label: S&P 500
change: +1.6% on Fri 27 Nov in a Black Friday half-day session, capping a +5.6% week, its biggest weekly gain since April 2025. Rally was broad: Dow +1.2% to 50,775 (+5.5% for the week), Russell 2000 small caps about 2,750 (+6.5% for the week), equal-weight S&P 500 fund +1.2% vs +1.6% for the cap-weighted one. Still about 4–5% below the 6 Oct record
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov (closes); The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov (Russell 2000, equal-weight)

label: Nasdaq Composite
change: +2.3% on Fri 27 Nov, and +6.7% for the week, after the Nasdaq-100 briefly hit bear-market territory on Wed 25 Nov. Nasdaq-100 +2.6% to 26,726
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov; The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov

label: Semiconductor index (SOX)
change: +4.7% on Fri 27 Nov from 8,775 on Wed 25 Nov, as chips led the rebound: Micron +7.6%, Broadcom +3.8%, TSMC ADR +3.2%, SanDisk about +16%. Still below its 17 Nov level of 9,643. Chip fund SMH +10% for the week
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov; The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov

label: Nvidia after Huang’s return
change: +0.8% on Fri 27 Nov, its first gain in three sessions, lagging the chip rebound. Still about 30% below a month ago. Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO on 23 Nov; the board investigation and a congressional probe continue, and Reuters has reported SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues (no finding of wrongdoing). S&P Global Ratings has put Nvidia’s AA rating on watch for a possible downgrade within 90 days over governance; Moody’s cut its outlook to stable on 18 Nov
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov; The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov; AP via BNN Bloomberg 26 Nov (S&P Global warning)

label: AMD after Nvidia’s CEO exit
change: +4.6% on Fri 27 Nov in the chip rebound (one source), after falls on 24–25 Nov. The Hunterbrook allegation about firmware reaching a blacklisted Chinese server maker is still unresolved (AMD denies wrongdoing)
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov; BigGo Finance 24 Nov

label: VIX volatility index
change: Fell about 11% to 23.8 on Fri 27 Nov, down about a third over the week from its spike. Still above its long-run average of about 20
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov; The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov

label: CoreWeave 5-yr default protection
change: No dated default-swap figure since Fri 20 Nov (1,233 bp intraday high). A 25 Nov Disruption Banking report put CoreWeave protection at 1,314 bp, a record, but gave no date, so the clock still uses 20 Nov. Shares rose about 12% over the week (+22% on Monday) to around US$43–44, after −11.9% on Tue 24 Nov. AI-debt ETFs that would bet against CoreWeave, Oracle and Meta credit have been filed with the SEC
source: Le Private Banker 20 Nov (default swap data); Disruption Banking 25 Nov; The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov

label: Oracle 5-yr default protection
change: No dated default-swap figure since Fri 20 Nov (about 328 bp, above this watch’s 300 bp bursting level). A 25 Nov Disruption Banking report cited a record 356 bp and SoftBank at 501 bp, without a date. Oracle shares rose about 5% over the week despite a 4.8% fall on Wed 25 Nov. Rated BBB-; no rating change reported
source: Le Private Banker 20 Nov (default swap data); Disruption Banking 25 Nov; The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov

label: Alphabet after its results
change: Closed −12.6% on Thu 29 Oct after its revenue and profit miss and −US$9.1bn Q3 free cash flow; ~US$280 on Fri, about 17% below a month ago
source: Saxo Options Brief 30 Oct; Yahoo Finance 30 Oct; Stocks Today 30 Oct

label: Meta equity raise
change: Largest equity raise ever, to fund AI build-out; includes preferred shares. Nvidia is investing US$3bn in it. Shares −1.6%
source: Reuters via MarketScreener; Yahoo Finance live; Kitco, 27 Oct

label: US investment-grade bond sales, 2026
change: An all-time annual record, passing 2020, driven by AI borrowing

label: US high-yield bond spread
change: 377 bp on Wed 25 Nov, from 372 bp on 24 Nov and 323 bp on 13 Nov: junk-bond spreads have widened about 55 bp in under two weeks. The Friday stock rally has not yet shown up in this series. Still well below crisis levels
source: ICE BofA US High Yield OAS via FRED, cited by The Glass Desk 27 Nov

label: Big-tech capex outlook
change: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but cracks are showing: analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google is cutting 2027 shipments of a Broadcom-designed AI chip by about a fifth (neither company has commented), and Alphabet sold bonds at wider spreads than in May. UBS estimates ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses. Megacaps fell 3.9% on average Fri 20 Nov (Meta −5.9%, Amazon −4.1%, Microsoft −2.8%, Alphabet −2.7%)
source: TECHi 20 Nov; GV Wire (Reuters) 5 Nov; Reuters via Yahoo Finance 4 Nov

label: US 10-yr Treasury yield
change: About 4.90% on Fri 27 Nov in a shortened session, up about 3–5 bp as money moved back into stocks. 2-yr about 4.66%, 30-yr about 5.29% (intraday). Official closing yields were not yet published
source: BigGo Finance 27 Nov (4.904%); Eurasia Business News 27 Nov (2-yr, 30-yr, intraday)

label: US Fed funds rate
change: A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is about 97–99% priced after October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% a year (core 3.3%) and Q3 growth was revised up to 4.3%. Markets expect another hike in January or early 2027. US November jobs data land at 12:30am Saturday 5 Dec Melbourne time; the Fed decision at 6am Thursday 10 Dec
source: CME FedWatch 26 Nov via Quackonomist (97.4%); Mitrade via FinanceFeeds 27 Nov (99.4%); BigGo Finance 27 Nov

label: Oil (WTI crude)
change: WTI settled at US$83.08 on Fri 27 Nov (−0.7% from Wednesday, −0.9% for the week). Brent fell 1.2% to US$95.44 but rose about 3% for the week, its first weekly gain in November, on attacks on tankers and Saudi facilities. OPEC+ is expected to hold output at Sunday’s meeting
source: Reuters via AOL 27 Nov; Political.org 27 Nov

label: US CPI inflation
change: October CPI +0.4% m/m (0.3% expected), core +0.3% for a third month. BLS did not publish annual rates because October 2025 data are missing. October PCE inflation, released 25 Nov, rose to 3.8% a year (core 3.3%)
source: BLS release 10 Nov; Yahoo Finance live 25 Nov (PCE)

label: Gold
change: Gold futures rose about 3.9% to around US$3,675 on Fri 27 Nov (+4.5% for the week), rebounding from a 15-month low; silver jumped about 6%. Metals rose with stocks, so no forced-selling signal
source: The Glass Desk weekly review 27 Nov (Yahoo front-month); FinanceFeeds 27 Nov; Eurasia Business News 27 Nov

label: Copper
change: About −4.8% to US$11,912/tonne overnight to Wed 25 Nov Melbourne time (about US$5.40/lb; London benchmark price, not the COMEX settle), about 17% below its September peak
